questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have many friends in Göteborg and my partner is Swedish so that played a big part. But I also wanted a university that could offer courses in what I am most interested in - which the university could.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I used the information centers to get help initially

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I don't know if there was much assistance at my arrival - but there were easy ways to seek it out for oneself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My situation doesn't apply to most because I lived with my partner.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Partille. They should perhaps know that the areas around Göteborg are super beautiful as well - if you are more into nature, then its both cheaper and nicer out there I think.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Doesn't apply to me.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because the registration is different than at UCPH, this was somewhat confusing. I didn't receive an email for registration to my course, but I found out that I had been automatically registered.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up for a course. Then you have to register as well in Ladok for course and exam. Then you have to be there on the first day, I think, to still be registered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The infocenters

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got both courses I wanted - so very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a bit confusing, so talk with the infocenters or write the teacher

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because of my interest in bacterial microbiology, there was not a lot of options for me, but the courses I got in molecular microbiology were very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MA both

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Especially one of the courses I took were very hands-on and gave a lot of freedom to design and execute our own experiments for 4-5 weeks. I have had one MA course at UCPH which had the same structure to a certain degree, but the course at GU was at another level in these regards.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Eukaryotic Molecular Microbiology and Prokaryotic Molecular Microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the Prokaryotic Molecular Microbiology - we had amazing teachers and a very cool project where we had a lot of freedom to make our own experimental designs and execute them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food has gotten very expensive in Sweden because of inflation. Organic product is very expensive compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My passion is environmental activism, and the university has no groups for this

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student unions seemed to be the major activity as far as I could see. There was one Free Palestine organisation as well, which was super good.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know. Just going out with other students I think.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The forests are great. If you are into climbing there is amazing climbing all around Göteborg area.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly got contact with the ones I had courses with

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I mostly appreciate the nature. Otherwise, Swedish people are very nice in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use the nature and areas all around Göteborg - Göteborg is placed in such a beautiful area. Buy a monthly transport card, otherwise it will get expensive. Remember to get Mecenat.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No its pretty similar to UCPH. Just watch all the intro-videos and attend the intro-meetings online. They are very informative.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My first course was amazing. And it has been great people attending the courses as well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Both courses I took were very intense. There was a lot more small assignments and constant evaluations. This was challenging, but also good to a certain extent. It forced everyone to be very involved.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
